question.text: If $A, B$ are two events such that $P(A \cup B) \geq \frac{3}{4}$ and $\frac{1}{8} \leq P(A \cap B) \leq \frac{3}{8},$ then

solution.text:
We know,
$$
P(A \cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A \cap B)
$$
$\Rightarrow P(A)+P(B)=P(A \cup B)+P(A \cap B)$
Given, $\quad \frac{3}{4} \leq P(A \cup B) \leq 1$
and $\quad \frac{1}{8} \leq P(A \cap B) \leq \frac{3}{8}$
So. $\quad \frac{7}{8} \leq P(A \cup B)+P(A \cap B) \leq \frac{11}{8}$
$\therefore P(A)+P(B) \geq \frac{7}{8}$ and $P(A)+P(B) \leq \frac{11}{8}$
